raw.assessment: The incumbent produces the intended course set in 32/40 exports and supports seven-minute median handling for 24 files with unchanged assignments. This supports retaining private CSV delivery while investigating exceptions; it does not isolate checking or import effort. Six affected exports coincide with assignment changes and two with renames, suggesting a selection or reconciliation problem without establishing causation. Limiting observation: zero cross-center rows excludes the recently split course, so it cannot establish isolation for that transition. Fast execution also limits a compute-speed explanation for replacement delays. Neither proposed change is yet shown to meet the next-40-export targets.

openings.claim: Using current assignments for a requested historical week may omit intended courses; renamed courses may instead be present but difficult to reconcile by name.
openings.delta: Distinguish incorrect row selection from correct rows perceived as absent before changing export logic.
openings.prediction: Assignment-change failures show missing expected course identities; rename-only failures show expected identities under unfamiliar labels. Correct identities in both conditions weaken this account.
openings.probe: With fabricated participants, replay unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split-course fixtures for a fixed requested week. Have consenting coordinators establish the intended roster, record disagreements with local timetables, and compare identities in selected rows with that roster. Include unauthorized-center sentinels and concurrent attendance entry.
assumptions: Stable identities are inspectable internally without changing the documented CSV.
Historical assignments may be unavailable; the probe does not assume a production repair is feasible within six days.

openings.claim: Does replacement delay mainly occur before execution, after file completion, or while establishing the correct requested scope?
openings.delta: Separate queue, delivery and correction delays before introducing private coordinator-triggered reruns.
openings.prediction: Long request-to-start intervals support a queue intervention; long completion-to-access intervals support delivery changes; scope revisions support correcting selection first.
openings.probe: Timestamp request, scope agreement, execution start/end and authorized download in short coordinator sessions. Keep names private and CSV unchanged. Gate any rerun implementation on the six-day and hosting limits and nonblocking attendance entry.
assumptions: Replacement stages can be observed without collecting participant names.
Reduced elapsed waiting need not reduce active handling time.

raw.assessment: The observations associate course changes with affected exports but do not establish causation. Outcome payment could favor preventing selection errors or removing replacement friction. Neither proposal has established six-day feasibility or achieved the success measures.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: pay the provider a fixed fee plus a bonus for the complete next-40-export cohort meeting all three success measures. This may motivate a private, center-and-week-scoped course manifest that preserves course identity across renames and assignment changes while retaining the documented CSV.
openings.delta: Reward maintained usable exports instead of job completion. Include failed, withheld and replacement exports in the originating week's accounting so omission cannot improve the score; independently establish intended courses rather than letting the provider redefine them.
openings.prediction: Against the incumbent, fabricated reassignment and rename cases would more often match coordinator-stated intended sets without increasing checking work. Split-course cases could expose a remaining identity or isolation failure.
openings.probe: In the first coordinator sessions, establish intended sets before showing exports; compare incumbent and manifest prototypes on fabricated unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split cases. Check exact sets, center isolation and active handling time while attendance entry continues. First verify historical mapping availability and scope implementation within six engineer-days and current hosting.
assumptions: Useful historical mappings exist or can be bounded within the budget.
Coordinators can resolve intended-set disagreements without substantial recurring work.

openings.claim: If the fixed fee includes every replacement and bonus eligibility still requires the original outcome thresholds, would the provider reduce coordinator effort through immediate private self-service regeneration, or merely transfer repair work to coordinators?
openings.delta: Internalizing replacement costs might encourage faster access, but also encourage hidden manual retries or suppressed support requests. Count every attempt and all coordinator correction work.
openings.prediction: The discriminator is reduced total active handling with unchanged correctness; shorter elapsed waits alone would indicate improved availability without demonstrated handling benefit.
openings.probe: Use second sessions to compare the incumbent replacement route with a fabricated-data regeneration prototype. Measure download, checking, correction and import time separately, plus waits, retries and final course-set accuracy. Retain private processing, schema and concurrent entry; bound resource use before implementation.
assumptions: Existing export execution can be safely exposed within the remaining budget.
Session measurements approximate routine coordinator work.

openings.claim: Current assignments may omit historical courses; renames may obscure present identities. Fixed fee plus cohort-outcome bonus could encourage a private center/week manifest.
openings.discriminator: Missing identities support selection error; unfamiliar labels support reconciliation error; correct identities weaken selection claims. Manifest must improve exact sets without extra checking.
openings.fit: Preserves privacy, CSV and concurrent entry; six-day/hosting feasibility uncertain.
openings.probe: First sessions: independently establish intended sets before exports, record timetable disagreements; compare incumbent/manifest on fabricated unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split courses, with unauthorized-center sentinels. Verify historical mappings, handling time and concurrent entry.
openings.uncertainty: Associations are not causal; mappings and affordable resolution of intended-set disputes are unproven.

openings.claim: Including every replacement in the fixed fee might motivate private regeneration, transfer repair work or suppress support requests.
openings.discriminator: Request-to-start delay suggests queue; completion-to-access suggests delivery; scope revisions suggest selection. Shorter waits alone do not demonstrate reduced active handling.
openings.fit: Preserves privacy, schema and concurrent entry; safe exposure and resource bounds unproven.
openings.probe: Second sessions: compare incumbent replacement and fabricated regeneration. Timestamp request, scope agreement, execution and download; measure checking, correction, downloading and importing separately, waits, all retries and final accuracy.
openings.uncertainty: Session effort may not represent routine work; hidden retries could erase gains.

lineage.reason: Queue, delivery and scope distinctions retained.
Replacement incentives and work-transfer risks retained.

post_distill.decision: Probe first; no demonstrated success. Gate implementation on six engineer-days/current hosting. Bonus requires complete next-40 cohort: median handling <=12 minutes, >=95% intended sets, zero cross-center records. Count failed, withheld and replacement exports against originating weeks, including all correction effort; independently establish intended sets.
